% A file of the document named like tex4ht's reading.4ht, read with
% \input before biblatex's reading style, whose files biblatex reads
% outside LaTeX's file hooks. As in the PDF, the file's text is in the
% page, with the bibliography's entry. tex4ht reads reading.4ht for the
% style. reading.4ht configures macros that the style no longer has, so
% the page shows that it was read only through \bbx@thebibitem, which it
% defines: the page's last sentence, which the PDF does not have. (The
% style's entry head is off: its two items give the entry's id twice.)
\documentclass{article}
\input{reading.ltx}
\usepackage[backend=bibtex,style=reading,entryhead=false]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{test-biblatex-authoryear.bib}
\begin{document}
Some text, as cited in \cite{book}. \ownreading
\printbibliography
\makeatletter
\ifdefined\bbx@thebibitem Read for the web.\fi
\makeatother
\end{document}
